entries.summary: Powers search over your own text. Works quietly in the background.
entries.description: A small helper that turns text into a compact numerical fingerprint, which is what powers local search, finding similar text, and organizing text on your Mac. It is tiny and runs quietly in the background. Each piece of text is limited to about 2,000 words.

entries.summary: Answers set questions about text in a fraction of a second.
entries.description: Answers set questions about a text - pick an option, rate on a scale, or say yes or no - with a probability for every answer. It writes no text, so it answers in a fraction of a second. Holds two models: laya-MLX-8bit for English, reading up to 512 tokens for each question (about 380 words), and laya-MLX-8bit-multilingual for other languages, reading up to 1,024 tokens. Longer text is cut to fit and the answer says so. Best with up to about 20 options for each question.

entries.summary: Answers many set questions about one text together, in a single pass.
entries.description: Answers set questions about a text - pick an option, rate on a scale, or say yes or no - with a probability for every answer, deciding all of a request's questions together in one pass. It writes no text. Reads up to 16,384 tokens for the whole request, its questions included (about 12,000 words); a longer text is cut to fit and the answer says so. Text only. Based on Cloudflare's Clef Flash, a 9B model.

entries.summary: A very small, fast model for simple tasks.
entries.description: A small, fast, all-around model for daily tasks - chatting, solving problems, using tools, and looking at pictures. It fits comfortably on most Macs, answers quickly, and keeps a large memory window for long conversations. Doubles as a lightweight assistant that helps bigger models respond faster.

entries.summary: A small model that balances speed and ability.
entries.description: A slightly larger all-around model for everyday use - chatting, reasoning, using tools, and understanding images. Runs on most Macs, balances speed and capability, and keeps a large memory window for long conversations and documents.

entries.summary: A large, careful model for harder writing and reasoning.
entries.description: A large, capable model that reads pictures and text and gives thoughtful answers. Best for harder work - writing, coding, and multi-step reasoning - when quality matters more than speed. This leaner version runs it on ordinary Macs without a noticeable drop in quality.

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: A light everyday assistant for writing, questions and photos, made for Macs with less memory.
entries.description: A capable everyday model that sees pictures and text, reasons before answering, and needs little memory. A strong all-rounder for common work - writing, coding, and understanding images. Ornith's own 4-bit weights with its original vision tower, at a lean size that runs comfortably on most Macs.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 4-bit (affine, group 64), vision tower at bf16

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The light everyday assistant with more of its detail kept, for a little more memory.
entries.description: A capable everyday model that sees pictures and text and reasons before answering, at higher fidelity. Ornith's own 6-bit weights with its original vision tower: slightly more faithful answers than the 4-bit version, for about 2 GB more memory.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 6-bit (affine, group 64), vision tower at bf16

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The light everyday assistant with a few key parts kept at 8 bits, between the 4-bit and 6-bit builds.
entries.description: A capable everyday model that sees pictures and text, reasons before answering, and needs little memory. This build keeps a few key parts of the model at 8 bits and the rest mostly at 4 or 5, so it sits between the 4-bit and 6-bit builds in size.

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The large Ornith with its original vision, for screenshots and documents.
entries.description: A large model that sees pictures and text and thinks carefully before answering. Best for harder work - reading screenshots and documents, writing, coding, and multi-step reasoning. Ornith's own 6-bit weights with its original vision tower, quick for its size because only a small part of it works on each word.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 6-bit (affine, group 64), 8-bit routers, bf16 vision tower

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The large Ornith with its original vision and a draft model built in: code about a tenth quicker.
entries.description: The same model as Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-MLX-6bit-vision, with a small draft model packed in. On an M5 Mac with room for the whole model, the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them all in one step, so code arrives about a tenth sooner while essays arrive about 7% later (measured on an M5 Pro Mac), and every word is still the large model's own choice. On other Macs, or with less memory, it runs just like the 6-bit vision build.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 6-bit (affine, group 64), bf16 vision, DFlash2 draft model

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: Ornith's 4-bit build with vision and its own draft model: the quickest Ornith 35B build for writing and code.
entries.description: The Ornith team's 4-bit Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B with its original vision put back, so it reads pictures, and their own draft model packed in. On an M5 Mac with room for the whole model, the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them in one step: it was the quickest Ornith 35B build measured on an M5 Pro Mac, at about 95 tokens a second for essays and 111 for code. Every word is still the large model's own. On other Macs it runs without the draft model.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 4-bit (affine, group 64), bf16 vision, DFlash draft model

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: Ornith's 6-bit build with vision and its own draft model: code about a fifth quicker.
entries.description: The Ornith team's 6-bit Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B with its original vision put back, so it reads pictures, and their own draft model packed in. On an M5 Mac with room for the whole model, the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them in one step: code arrives about a fifth sooner and essays at about the same pace (measured on an M5 Pro Mac). Every word is still the large model's own. On other Macs it runs without the draft model.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 6-bit (affine, group 64), bf16 vision, DFlash draft model

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The large Ornith with its original vision, for screenshots and documents.
entries.description: The highest-precision build of the large Ornith model that sees pictures and text and thinks carefully before answering. Best for harder work when quality matters most. Ornith's own 8-bit weights with its original vision tower, favoring quality over fitting smaller Macs.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 8-bit (affine, group 64), vision tower at bf16

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The large Ornith that sees, laid out to stream from the SSD on Macs with less memory.
entries.description: The same model as Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-MLX-8bit-vision, with every weight unchanged, stored so each expert can be read from the SSD in one step. Pick it when your Mac has less memory than the model: with 10 GB set aside it writes about 40% faster than the regular build. With enough memory to hold the whole model, both run the same.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 8-bit (affine, group 64), bf16 vision, Astro Atlas layout

entries.summary: The large Ornith with its original vision and a draft model built in, for M5 Macs with room to spare.
entries.description: The same model as Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-MLX-8bit-vision, with a small draft model packed in. On an M5 Mac with room for the whole model, the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them all in one step, so answers can arrive sooner, though its speed is not measured yet (a 48 GB Mac cannot hold it whole), and every word is still the large model's own choice. On other Macs, or with less memory, it runs just like the 8-bit vision build.
entries.quantization_label: MLX 8-bit (affine, group 64), bf16 vision, DFlash2 draft model

entries.summary: Turns a written description into a picture.
entries.description: The full-precision original of the FLUX.2 Klein 4B 4-bit image generator: the same model, all on your Mac, from a download about three times larger.

entries.summary: Turns a written description into a picture.
entries.description: A local image generator that turns a written description into one high-quality image, all on your Mac - no uploads, and no internet needed for the drawing itself.

entries.summary: A second picture maker to try beside FLUX.
entries.description: A local image generator that turns a written description into one clean image on your Mac, with no uploads and no internet needed for the drawing itself.

entries.summary: The heavy thinker for coding, long writing and complex reasoning.
entries.description: A large, powerful model for the hard jobs - long writing, complex reasoning, coding, and reading pictures. This leaner version keeps strong quality while fitting ordinary Macs. Expect thoughtful answers over fast ones.

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The heavy thinker with its draft model built in: writing about a fifth quicker, code about 40% quicker.
entries.description: The same large model as Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-OptiQ-4bit, with a small draft model packed in. On an M5 Mac the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them all in one step, so essays arrive about a fifth sooner and code about 40% sooner (measured on an M5 Pro Mac), and every word is still the large model's own choice. On other Macs, or with less memory, it runs just like the OptiQ build.
entries.quantization_label: OptiQ 4/8-bit (affine, group 64) with a DFlash2 draft model

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: The heavy thinker with more of its detail kept, for Macs with a little more memory.
entries.description: The same large model as Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-OptiQ-4bit, with more of each layer kept at 8 bits, so it needs about 4 GB more memory. For long writing, complex reasoning, coding, and reading pictures.

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: Built for code. Strong at finding and fixing bugs in real projects.
entries.description: A large, coding-focused model built from Ornith 1.5. It reads code and text, reasons through multi-step problems, and uses tools to work through real software tasks - strong at finding and fixing bugs. Runs on ordinary Macs with a lean 6-bit compression that keeps quality high for serious work.

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: Uncensored. For adults doing security research.
entries.description: An uncensored version of Tiel Coder for adults doing security research or unrestricted coding work. It is built from an abliterated Ornith 1.5 and will go along with requests other models refuse, including harmful ones, so it is not suitable for young people and is best run on a sandboxed setup you watch. It reads code, text and images, reasons through multi-step problems, and uses tools, with a lean 6-bit compression that keeps quality high.

entries.summary: A large all-round model that reads pictures, with its draft model built in.
entries.description: Qwen 3.8 27B in a 4-bit build with a small draft model packed in. A large, capable model that reads pictures and text, reasons before answering, and calls tools for agentic work. On an M5 Mac the draft model guesses the next few words and the large model checks them all in one step, so answers can arrive sooner, and every word is still the large model's own choice. On other Macs, with less memory, or when a message has a picture in it, it runs just like the plain 4-bit build.
entries.quantization_label: 4-bit affine (group 64), bf16 vision tower, DFlash2 draft model

measured_speed.measured_on: Mac with an M5 Pro and 48 GB

entries.summary: A 27B model squeezed into 8 GB. Text only.
entries.description: A 27B dense ternary model folded into a 2-bit pack. Every rotated projection applies its Hadamard transform at run time, so the compressed weights serve full-precision-quality chat with 48 gated-delta layers and 16 full-attention layers.
entries.quantization_label: 2-bit ternary affine (group 128) with folded Hadamard transforms

entries.summary: The same squeezed model, paired with a helper that speeds it up.
entries.description: A 27B dense ternary model folded into a 2-bit Hadamard pack and paired with a DFlash2 block-diffusion draft model for speculative decoding. The folded ternary weights serve full-precision chat quality, while the draft model accelerates generation by proposing tokens the main model verifies. Text-only, built on Qwen 3.8 27B.
entries.quantization_label: 2-bit ternary affine (group 128) with folded Hadamard transforms

entries.summary: The largest model in the catalog. Text only.
entries.description: The largest model in the catalog, built for the heaviest writing, reasoning, and coding work. This 2-bit mixed-precision build is the leanest way to run the full Ornith 122B - it takes about 37.9 GB on disk, and on a Mac with less memory than that it reads part of itself from the SSD, so replies are slower. Favors deep, thoughtful answers over fast ones. Reads text only.

entries.summary: Reads text aloud in natural American English voices.
entries.description: Reads English text aloud and answers with a WAV file. Offers 20 American English voices (af_heart is the default) and can speak from a quarter to four times its natural pace. Speaks a whole sentence in one pass, several times faster than the audio plays. Its other voices expect British English or other languages and are not offered. Based on Kokoro-82M, an 82M-parameter StyleTTS2 model.

entries.summary: Reads text aloud in one natural English voice, from a very small model.
entries.description: Reads English text aloud and answers with a WAV file, in one voice at its natural pace. At 31M parameters it is the smallest speech model in the catalog, and it reads words it has never seen without spelling them out. Based on Gradium's Phonon 31M.
